plan: judge-a everywhere, people see its flags and unsure verdicts, half of inform spot-checked
about: Reference solution for Exercise 15. Other plans can pass; the test checks the budget, the limit, and the evidence.

evidence.claim: On the holdout split, every draft judge-a got wrong was low-confidence except one sarcastic inform reply.
evidence.command: python3 -m returns_eval calibrate judge-a judge-b --split holdout

evidence.claim: judge-a flagged no fine drafts on holdout, so flag reviews are cheap; judge-b flagged 5 polite refusals.
evidence.command: python3 -m returns_eval calibrate judge-a judge-b --split holdout

evidence.claim: The drafts come from candidate-v2, a script, so judge-a's self-preference for sim-model replies doesn't apply here.

why: judge-a with unsure verdicts sent to people reaches every holdout problem except sarcasm in inform, so people spot-check half of inform. That keeps expected misses at 3 a week, under the limit of 5, for about $170 a week. Monthly relabeling keeps the error rates current. If drafts ever come from the sim-model family, switch to judge-b.
